title: World War I and the Great Depression
note: Drafted for Prompt 12 (Unit 6). Every lesson is a draft until a person reviews it (content/course/README.md).

listen.explanationKey: Name one war fought by the United States in the 1900s.
facts: The United States fought five wars in the 1900s that are on the test: World War I, World War II, the Korean War, the Vietnam War and the Persian Gulf War.
World War I was fought mostly in Europe. The United States joined in 1917 because Germany attacked U.S. ships. It joined the Allied Powers: England, France, Italy and Russia.

World War II (the United States joined in 1941) was fought against Germany, Italy and Japan. The Korean War (1950) and the Vietnam War (the 1960s) were fought to stop communism. The Persian Gulf War (1991) forced Iraq out of Kuwait.
Tip: the years of all five wars start with 19, so they belong to the 1900s.
Under the Constitution, Congress has the power to declare war.

facts: A depression is a long time when businesses close and many people have no work. The Great Depression was the longest economic recession in modern history.
It started with the stock market crash of 1929, called the Great Crash.
Many banks closed, and millions of families lost their jobs, homes and savings. People waited in long lines for free food, called bread lines.
It lasted about ten years, until World War II.
